newsitem.title: IRAN: Strong aftershock jolts Iran quake area, kills one.
newsitem.headline: Strong aftershock jolts Iran quake area, kills one.

text.p: A strong aftershock hit villages devastated by an earthquake in eastern Iran, flattening more houses and killing one person, the Iranian news agency IRNA said on Wednesday.

The aftershock measuring 5.6 on the Richter scale, the strongest of 250 recorded since Saturday's force 7.1 quake, jolted the towns of Qaen and Birjand and surrounding areas on Tuesday, the agency said.
It killed one person and destroyed 10 houses in a village already badly damaged by Saturday's quake which killed 1,560 people and made 50,000 homeless, IRNA said.
An earthquake measuring 4.2 on the Richter scale jolted the northwestern province of East Azerbaijan on Wednesday, but there was no immediate word on casualties, the agency said earlier.
The epicentre of Wednesday's quake was 100 km (60 miles) northeast of the provincial capital of Tabriz, it said.
Earthquakes of force four or more are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area.
International aid continued to arrive in quake-prone Iran, where emergency food stocks have been depleted after three major quakes this year.

The Red Crescent in the quake-stricken Khorasan province said on Wednesday 15 planes carrying relief supplies from Egypt, Syria, Oman, Jordan, Kuwait, France, Tajikistan and Pakistan landed in the provincial capital Mashhad on Tuesday, IRNA said.
The supplies included tents, blankets, rice, powdered milk, canned food, medicine, biscuits, sugar and dates.
More aid was coming from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, the agency said.

Algeria's Red Crescent said on Wednesday that it would contribute $100,000 to help the quake victims. Algeria broke diplomatic ties with Iran in 1993, accusing Iran of supporting Moslem rebels fighting the Algerian government.

In Geneva, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said on Tuesady it had raised seven million Swiss francs ($4.6 million) towards its 12 million Swiss franc appeal issued on Monday to help the quake victims.
The money was raised from four governments -- Britain, Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway -- and from 13 national Red Cross or Red Crescent societies.
Several countries made pledges or said they had sent aid, including Iran's arch-foe the United States and European Union states involved in a diplomatic row with Tehran.
